Commentary.Commentary: We are back and the good news is that the English first innings will start right away! The umpires are back out in the middle and the Lankan players are seen in a huddle with the coach giving some final words of wisdom. It will be the new opening pair of Ben Duckett and Dan Lawrence to open the innings for England. Also, it will be spin to get things underway with the light and skipper Dhananjaya de Silva has taken the new ball himself. Let's go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

With 236 runs on the board, Sri Lanka will be slightly disappointed with their batting display. They now face the challenge of making the most of the overhead conditions and the remaining session to make a significant impact with the ball. The pitch remains conducive to batting, and England will be eager to build a substantial first-innings lead and tighten their grip on this match. However, with the fading light, the umpires take another reading before going off and the possibility of further play on Day 1 rests completely on the light. Dhananjaya de Silva might opt to start with spin but whether the umpires allow it or not remains to be seen. Join us in a bit to find out.

Milan Rathnayake continued his impressive debut into the final session, reaching a well-deserved half-century with strong support from Vishwa Fernando, ensuring the scoreboard kept ticking for Sri Lanka. England's pace attack remained the highlight, with Chris Woakes and Gus Atkinson leading the charge, taking three and two wickets respectively. The rest of the bowling unit also delivered disciplined performances. However, they faltered slightly in the later stages of the second session and the start of the third session, allowing Sri Lanka to accumulate some valuable runs.

What began as a struggle and persisted through much of the second session saw a remarkable turnaround from Sri Lanka's lower order, who showed tremendous resilience to push the score to 236 runs, a recovery that seemed unlikely when they were teetering at a much lower total. Despite this late resistance, England will still be pleased with their bowling performance on a pitch that offered minimal assistance. Their relentless attack was justly rewarded, taking full advantage of the lackluster batting from Sri Lanka's top and middle order.

OUT! RUN OUT! A mixup against the run of play and Sri Lanka get bundled out for 236 runs. Joe Root bowls it nice and full on the stumps, Vishwa Fernando tucks it in front of Ollie Pope at mid-wicket before setting off for a quick single. Asitha Fernando sends him back, leaving Vishwa stranded halfway down the track. Pope quickly collects the ball and throws it to keeper Jamie Smith, who swiftly knocks the bails off. Despite a desperate dive from Vishwa Fernando, he was well short of the crease, bringing Sri Lanka's innings to a close.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the third and final session on Day 1! The umpires have taken their places out in the middle as the English players stride out to the middle, hoping that it will be a quick jog back to the dressing room. Milan Rathnayake and Vishwa Fernando are all set to resume their stay and keep the fight going for Sri Lanka in this first innings. It will be Shoaib Bashir to continue from the James Anderson end after the break. Let's go...
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

Right then! The Lankan tail-enders would like to pursue their partnership for the next couple of hours. They would certainly want to survive till the end of the day and keep their scoreboard ticking. On the other side, the English bowlers would like to wrap things up as quickly as possible. Stay tuned, as an enthralling final session on Day 1 will be up next shortly.

The English bowlers were doing exceptional to pick up wickets on a regular event but it was a huge task for them to hunt DDS down. They tried to attack with spin as well as pace on the opposite ends but they were just not finding their results. There was no visible swing lately and hence, the pitch evolved into a surface where patience and application were crucial for both the batting and bowling sides. But Shoaib Bashir helped his team to get the most wanted breakthrough and won the game of patience late in the second session.

However, the storms were blowing all hopes for Sri Lanka, but their skipper stood out tall to defend his wicket and kept on caressing the deliveries to trigger the scoreline towards the 200-run mark. Dhananjaya de Silva outstandingly paved his way from a crumbled situation and also achieved his 15th test half-century in Test cricket format. His inning has been very crucial for his nation as he was the only batter left in their batting lineup. He also got lucky in the 41st over as the English keeper, Jamie Smith missed out on the stumping which might turn out as exorbitant for England. Milan Rathnayake also did well to passively support his skipper and kept rotating their strike to form a rugged partnership of 63 runs before DDS eventually got out.

TEA, DAY 1 - Session Summary - 27 overs, 98 runs, 3 wickets. The start after the Lunch break was once again in the favour of the Three Lions. Just after a couple of overs, Chris Woakes picks his third wicket of the innings in the 29th over dismissing Kamindu Mendis. Prabath Jayasuriya walked up in the middle as six-man down but no positive results were popping up from the Lankan batters. Prabath got a golden lifeline in the 34th over but failed to capitalize on it but was dismissed in the very same over.
Goes full and straight, Milan Rathnayake does well to dig it out back to the bowler and that will be TEA ON DAY 1!

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the post-Lunch session on Day 1! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of England. Sri Lankan skipper, Dhananjaya de Silva is all set to resume his stay on the crease alongside Kamindu Mendis. It will be Gus Atkinson who will get proceedings underway with the ball after the interval. Let's play...
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

Right then, plenty of action in the first session but this is just the beginning and now both teams will look to find some consistency in the post-Lunch session. England will look to get through to the Lankan tail whereas DDS and Co will look to lose as few wickets as possible while mustering up some vital runs. Join us at 12.40 pm GMT for the second session on Day 1.

Dinesh Chandimal continued to hold up one end as skipper Dhananjaya de Silva took on the mantle of keeping the scoreboard ticking and another budding partnership was formed only to be broken less than 10 minutes before the Lunch break as a ball from Shoaib Bashir kept really low and caught Chandimal on the pads right in front of the stumps. This halted Sri Lanka yet again and they went into the interval having lost half their side.

However, Mark Wood then came into the attack and he started firing on all cylinders right away, bowling in excess of 145 kph for fun and he made the ball really shoot off the deck. Kusal Mendis was on the receiving end of a nasty delivery that caught him on the already injured right thumb and the Lankans had to rebuild yet again.

The day began with fairly blue skies but the English opening bowlers made the new ball talk well. Chris Woakes kept hitting the right lengths and Gus Atkinson used the scrambled seam to good effect. The pair had the opposition reeling at 6/3 after which there was some resistance. Kusal Mendis and the experienced Dinesh Chandimal then stitched together a steady stand as the new ball bowlers wore and Mendis then took on the inexperienced Matthew Potts.

DAY 1, LUNCH BREAK! A brisk first session on Day 1 of the first Test match and at the end of it, hosts England have done a huge amount of damage after Sri Lanka opted to bat first. Five wickets fell and it didn't even look that difficult of a pitch to bat on with 80 runs being scored in 25 overs.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks! In the opening hour of play, England have dominated, claiming three quick wickets and putting Sri Lanka on the defensive. With the weather forecast suggesting cloudy overhead conditions throughout the day, the toss could play a crucial role in this match. While England may enter the match as favourites, Sri Lanka have the potential to spring a surprise. By executing their plans right, they could put on an impressive performance against a revamped English side, which feels like a nice opportunity that might play to their advantage. This could also be their moment to break a decade-long drought and secure a Test victory against England. With anticipation mounting by the minute, stay glued as the all-important toss is just moments away.

On the other hand, Sri Lanka, with a packed Test calendar ahead, will be eager to kick off their campaign on a positive note. Captain Dhananjaya de Silva faces a daunting task against an English side brimming with momentum and confidence. This team will need to display resilience and grit in challenging English conditions. Although a loss in their warm-up game against an inexperienced England Lions might have dented their morale slightly, Sri Lanka remains a side not to be underestimated. The squad boasts considerable depth and talent and will need to assess and adapt to the conditions quickly to make their presence felt. Sri Lanka has chosen to field debutant Milan Rathnayake alongside Asitha Fernando and Vishwa Fernando to spearhead the pace attack while relying on a lone spinner, Prabath Jayasuriya, who is expected to become increasingly effective as the game progresses.

England face a significant setback with the absence of Ben Stokes, ruled out due to a recent injury. His absence could prove to be a major blow to a side that has been consistently proactive and dominant in Test cricket over the past couple of years. However, all eyes will now be on Ollie Pope, the new stand-in captain, who bears the responsibility of leading the team. It will be fascinating to see how he marshals this troop. Despite Stokes’ absence, his presence around the squad may still influence England to maintain their aggressive approach and assert their dominance. Matthew Potts also returns to the side after more than a year, providing him with a golden opportunity to make an impact. Additionally, the new opening pair of Dan Lawrence and Ben Duckett will be closely watched.
